title: 'El Mansito,' Alleged CJNG Extortion Network Leader, Killed in Morelia Confrontation
detail: On September 26, 2026, Michoacán state Guardia Civil personnel conducting a surveillance/intelligence operation on Avenida Periodismo in Morelia located Rafael 'N,' alias 'El Mansito,' a priority target wanted on active warrants for qualified homicide and aggravated kidnapping. Authorities said he drew a handgun and fired on officers, who returned fire, killing him at the scene; no security personnel were injured. State intelligence reports identified him as a leader of a CJNG-linked extortion network operating across Michoacán and neighboring Guanajuato, tracing his criminal career back to 2008 when he was recruited as a lookout ('halcón') for La Familia Michoacana in southern Morelia before rising to manage drug-sale points and cartel safehouses; he had previously been arrested in 2010 and sentenced to 30+ years in 2021 on unlawful-detention, drug-trafficking and exclusive-military-ammunition charges.

media.caption: 'El Mansito,' alleged CJNG extortion network leader, killed in a Morelia confrontation with state Guardia Civil

confidenceReason: The confrontation, death and outstanding homicide/kidnapping warrants are confirmed by Michoacán state security officials and corroborated by three independent Tier-2 outlets; his specific CJNG affiliation and rank rest on state intelligence characterization rather than a court finding.

title: Alleged CJNG Colombia Liaison 'El Mexicano' Captured in Medellín, Wanted by DEA Since 2015
detail: On September 26, 2026, Colombian authorities — the Policía Metropolitana del Valle de Aburrá, the Dirección de Investigación Criminal (Dijín), police intelligence (Dipol), Interpol and the Fiscalía General de la Nación — captured Freddy Chacón, alias 'El Mexicano,' at a luxury residence in Medellín. Colombian officials identified him as an alleged liaison between CJNG and 'La Eme' (the Mexican Mafia) in Colombia, allegedly overseeing a scheme in which the group operated since at least 2022 and moved more than 300 migrants out of Colombia, and allegedly paying $10,000–$15,000 per month to local criminal organizations for territorial protection. He has been sought by the U.S. DEA since 2015 and, according to FBI and U.S. Marshals Service records cited by authorities, has prior convictions for aggravated assault with a firearm, weapons violations and extortive kidnapping. He was placed at the disposal of Colombia's Migration Authority pending a possible extradition process to the United States; computers, phones, hard drives, USB drives and documents were seized at the scene.

media.caption: Freddy Chacón, alias 'El Mexicano,' captured in Medellín, Colombia, on suspicion of acting as a CJNG liaison

confidenceReason: The capture, location and DEA interest since 2015 are confirmed by Colombian authorities and corroborated by three independent Tier-2 outlets; the specific characterization of him as a CJNG (rather than solely Mexican Mafia) liaison rests on Colombian prosecutorial claims pending further investigation.
